Key observations from test image:
- Prominent interveinal yellowing (green veins, yellow interveinal tissue)
- Brown necrotic lesion on left side of leaf
- Leaf is flat (not curled)
- Overall chlorosis pattern

Top candidates: Verticillium_Wilt (interveinal yellowing), Leaf_Mold, Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus. Let me check references.

Verticillium_Wilt reference shows a strong match — bottom-right image has the same interveinal yellowing with prominent green veins pattern. Leaf_Mold doesn't match (needs velvety spots). Let me check TYLCV to rule it out.

TYLCV ruled out — shows curled, small leaves, not what we see here.

**Final analysis:**
- Test image: flat leaf, prominent green veins with interveinal yellowing, brown necrotic lesion on one side
- Verticillium_Wilt reference (bottom-right): exact same pattern — interveinal chlorosis with dark green veins prominent, yellow tissue between
- The brown necrotic area aligns with V-shaped/margin lesions of Verticillium
- No powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew), no discrete spots (rules out Septoria/Bacterial Spot), no curling (rules out TYLCV)
